function: Learned sub-channel allocation by a pointer network plus DNN power-allocation prediction in a LEO-satellite downlink; convex optimization then fixes the final power (pp. 5-9).
system: Ka-band (20-30 GHz) downlink, K LEO satellites (500-2000 km) to one ground station over N subchannels; antennas given only by effective area; no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: Pointer network (LSTM encoder-decoder) trained online by actor-critic policy-gradient RL; two-hidden-layer fully connected DNN trained supervised on convex-optimizer outputs with experience replay (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Custom simulated gains (antenna areas, distance 500-2000 km, frequency, random attenuation 0-40 dB, Table I ranges); no standard model, public dataset or measurement (pp. 4, 10-11).
test_conditions: Online training frame by frame on random gains and satellite parameters; results reported per (N, K) case on the same stream; no held-out or unseen scenario (pp. 7, 11).
baselines: Non-learned: Opt-Greedy (best average gain), Opt-RDS (random allocation). Learned: Opt-DNN [30] (fully connected DNN with quantization); all with convex power allocation (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Sum weighted transmission data (information-freshness-weighted downloaded data) per frame and averaged over K and N; DNN training loss (pp. 10-13).
q1_support: p. 10: "randomly distributed in the range presented in Table I" The channel gains come from the authors' own model with random attenuation; no 3GPP TR 38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 7: "Such iterations repeat thereafter as the input of each time frame is different" The networks learn online on a stream of random frames; no model trained under one K, N or channel setting is tested on another.
q3_support: p. 10: "Opt-Greedy: Each sub-channel is allocated to the satellites corresponding to the max average channel gain" (non-learned) and "Opt-DNN [30]: The Opt-DNN algorithm obtains the channel allocation by applying a fully connected DNN" (learned); Figs. 5-9 compare the sum weighted transmission data.
q4_support: p. 5: "is time-consuming, and we will propose a more efficient method" is only a qualitative remark about CVX; no complexity order, operation count, parameter count or runtime of the proposed algorithms is reported (Table II, p. 11, lists hyperparameters only).
q5_support: p. 10: "randomly distributed in the range presented in Table I" The data are generated by the authors' simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included as area 6: learned sub-channel allocation and power prediction for a LEO satellite downlink, counted as physical-layer resource and power control in satellite links; the final power comes from convex optimization (p. 5). The objective weights information freshness. The system model calls the link mainly free space optical (p. 4) while the simulation uses Ka band 20-30 GHz (p. 10). Opt-DNN is a DROO-style fully connected DNN [30] applied to the same channel allocation problem, which I take as the learned baseline.
